title: sdks: unify auth/retries and streaming ergonomics across Python/TypeScript/Go; parity fixes and version bumps
author: Jordan Patel
release_notes: Unified SDK auth/retry behavior across Python/TS/Go; improved streaming ergonomics and parity; bumped SDK package versions to v1.97.1; small bugfixes for Go and Python streaming clients.
description: Motivation: Inconsistent auth retry semantics and streaming ergonomics across our SDKs have caused developer confusion and subtle production bugs. This PR unifies auth token refresh/retry behavior, standardizes streaming API ergonomics (client-side backpressure and reconnect handling), and applies parity fixes across Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs. The change set also includes coordinated version bumps to v1.97.1 for published packages. What changed: 1) Auth/Retry: centralized retry policy (exponential backoff with jitter), transparent token refresh hook, uniform 429/5xx handling and idempotency guidance. 2) Streaming ergonomics: unified streaming client interfaces, added explicit Close/Stop helpers, improved reconnection logic with jitter and max attempts, and consistent event names across languages. 3) Parity fixes: aligned param names, normalized error types, and fixed a missing metadata header in Go client for function-calling streaming. 4) Version bumps: python sdk -> 1.97.1, typescript sdk -> 1.97.1, go sdk -> v1.97.1. Backwards compatibility: all APIs are additive; default retry and streaming behavior is backward compatible but opt-in toggles are provided for legacy ergonomics. Testing: unit tests added for retry backoff, streaming reconnect scenarios, and integration smoke tests against the mock inference gateway. Release impact: No breaking changes expected for typical usage; recommend customers pinning older versions to test migration. Checklist: - [x] Implement shared retry logic in common/sdk-core - [x] Add token refresh hook and sample in examples/ - [x] Harmonize streaming client APIs across languages - [x] Add unit/integration tests - [x] Update changelogs and bump package versions - [x] CI green across Python/TS/Go CI lanes
